body.para: Purpose
Opens a table and its indexes, or closes a table, using the syntax of the FoxPro dialect. This is the FoxPro version of the USE command.
Syntax

USE <TableName> [IN <WorkArea> | <Alias>]
[ONLINE] [ADMIN] [AGAIN] [NOREQUERY [<nDataSession>]] [NODATA]
[INDEX <IndexFile1> [, <IndexFile2> ...]]
[ORDER [TAG] <OrderName> [OF <IndexFile>]] [ASCENDING | DESCENDING]
[ALIAS <Alias>] [EXCLUSIVE | SHARED] [NOUPDATE] [CONNSTRING <ConnectionString>]
USE IN <WorkArea> | <Alias>
Arguments
<TableName>The name of the table to open. When the table is not found in the current directory the search path is used (see SET PATH).

AGAINOpens the table again in a new work area, while it is also open in another work area. The new work area uses the same shared/exclusive and read-only mode as the work area where the table is already open.
INDEX <IndexFile1>, ...Opens the specified index files together with the table.

ORDER [TAG] <OrderName> [OF <IndexFile>]Selects the controlling order after the table has been opened. The order can be a tag name from a compound index file (CDX), or the name of an order in the index file that is specified in the OF clause.
ASCENDING | DESCENDINGChanges the direction of the controlling order. This is only done when the ORDER clause is also specified.

ALIAS <Alias>The alias for the table. When this clause is omitted, the alias is the name of the table without path and extension. When that alias is already in use by another work area then a unique alias is generated.
EXCLUSIVEOpens the table for exclusive use. By default the table is opened as set by SET EXCLUSIVE.
SHAREDOpens the table for shared use.
NOUPDATEOpens the table read-only.
ONLINE, ADMIN, NOREQUERY, NODATA, CONNSTRINGThese clauses are only relevant for remote views and are accepted for compatibility, but ignored.
Remarks

The FoxPro version of the command uses the DBFVFP RDD as the default driver, so the table can be a DBF with the FoxPro extensions (null fields, auto-increment fields, DateTime and Currency fields and so on).

USE IN <WorkArea> closes the table in the specified work area. The command USE without any clauses closes the table in the current work area, as described in USE. CLOSE IN <WorkArea> has the same effect as USE IN.
Examples

USE Customers ALIAS Cust SHARED NOUPDATE
USE Customers AGAIN IN 0 ALIAS Cust2 ORDER TAG LastName
USE IN Cust2
See Also
USE, CLOSE, CLOSE TABLES, SELECT, DbUseAreaFox(), DbCloseArea(), DbSetIndex()
